questions.question: Describe the function of the middle ear.
questions.solution_html: • Describe the function of the middle ear. / ● Transmission of sound: Transfers sound vibrations from the tympanic membrane (eardrum) to the inner ear through the ossicles — malleus, incus, and stapes. ● Amplification: The ossicles amplify the sound vibrations to overcome the resistance of the fluid in the inner ear. ● Pressure equalization: The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx and helps equalize air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. ● Protection: The tensor tympani and stapedius muscles protect the inner ear from loud sounds by dampening excessive vibrations. (Any 2 points: (1 mark) each)

questions.question: A woman with PCOD complains of infertility. How do assisted reproductive techniques apply in her management?
questions.solution_html: • A woman with PCOD complains of infertility. How do assisted reproductive techniques apply in her management? / ● Ovulation induction therapy – Use of drugs like Clomiphene citrate , Letrozole , or Gonadotropins to stimulate ovulation. ● Intrauterine insemination (IUI) – Washed sperm are directly introduced into the uterus near the time of ovulation. ● In vitro fertilization (IVF) – Eggs are collected, fertilized in the lab, and the resulting embryos are transferred to the uterus. ● Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) – A single sperm is injected directly into an egg; used when sperm count or motility is low. ● Laparoscopic ovarian drilling (LOD) – A surgical technique to destroy androgen-producing tissue, improving ovulation. ● Cryopreservation of embryos or oocytes – Useful for preserving fertility if repeated cycles are needed. ● Lifestyle modification support – Though not ART itself, weight reduction and insulin-sensitizing drugs like metformin enhance ART success. (Any two methods with explanations or four methods mentioned briefly can be given full marks.)

questions.question: Write short notes on Graves’ disease.
questions.solution_html: • Write short notes on Graves’ disease. / ● Graves’ disease is an autoimmune disorder causing hyperthyroidism. ● The body produces TSH receptor antibodies that overstimulate the thyroid gland. ● Leads to excess secretion of thyroid hormones (T ₃ and T ₄ ). ● Symptoms: weight loss, heat intolerance, rapid heartbeat, tremors, anxiety, and exophthalmos (bulging eyes). ● Treatment: antithyroid drugs, radioactive iodine therapy, or partial thyroidectomy. questions.question: Explain how nociceptors are involved in the perception of pain through the skin.
questions.solution_html: • Explain how nociceptors are involved in the perception of pain through the skin. / ● Nociceptors are specialized sensory receptors in the skin that detect painful or damaging stimuli such as extreme heat, pressure, or chemicals. ● When activated, they generate nerve impulses that travel through sensory neurons to the spinal cord. ● These impulses are then relayed to the brain, particularly the thalamus and somatosensory cortex, where pain is perceived. ● This mechanism helps the body recognize and respond to potential harm, promoting protective actions like withdrawal from the source of injury. questions.question: Describe the important functions of endocrine system in our body.
questions.solution_html: • Describe the important functions of the endocrine system in our body. / ● Regulates metabolism: Controls energy production and nutrient use through hormones like insulin and thyroxine. ● Maintains homeostasis: Keeps internal conditions stable, including blood pressure, temperature, and water balance. ● Controls growth and development: Growth hormone and thyroid hormones promote body growth and tissue development. ● Regulates reproduction: Hormones like estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone control sexual development and fertility. ● Coordinates stress response: Adrenal hormones such as cortisol and adrenaline help the body respond to stress. ● Regulates mood and behavior: Hormones influence emotions, sleep, and mental well-being. ● Regulates blood glucose levels: Insulin and glucagon maintain normal blood sugar balance. ● Controls calcium and bone metabolism: Parathyroid hormone and calcitonin regulate calcium levels and bone strength. ● Influences circadian rhythm: Melatonin from the pineal gland controls sleep–wake cycles. ● Aids in digestion: Hormones like gastrin, secretin, and cholecystokinin regulate digestive processes. ● Supports immune function: Thymosin promotes immune cell development. ● Regulates blood pressure and fluid balance: Aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone (ADH) maintain water and salt balance. ● Promotes cell repair and regeneration: Growth factors assist in tissue maintenance and healing. ● Integrates with the nervous system: Works with the hypothalamus to coordinate body responses to internal and external changes . (Explain any 4 points with brief explanations – (4 marks) or mention any correct 6 points- (4 marks)

questions.question: Explain the interaction between sympathetic nervous system and adrenal medulla in stress.
questions.solution_html: • Explain the interaction between the sympathetic nervous system and adrenal medulla in stress. / ● During stress, the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is activated as part of the “fight or flight” response. ● The SNS stimulates the adrenal medulla (inner part of the adrenal gland) through sympathetic nerve fibers. ● The adrenal medulla then releases epinephrine (adrenaline) and norepinephrine (noradrenaline) into the bloodstream. ● These hormones increase heart rate, blood pressure, respiration, and glucose release, preparing the body to handle stress. ● This shows a close coordination where the SNS provides rapid nerve stimulation, and the adrenal medulla ensures a prolonged hormonal effect to manage stress efficiently. (Give full marks for relevant explanation)

questions.question: Discuss how hormonal changes in the ovaries prepare the female body for fertilization and implantation.
questions.solution_html: • Discuss how hormonal changes in the ovaries prepare the female body for fertilization and implantation. / ● Follicular phase: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) promotes the growth of ovarian follicles, which secrete estrogen. Estrogen thickens the endometrium and prepares the cervix for sperm entry. ● Ovulation: A surge in luteinizing hormone (LH) triggers the release of an egg (ovum) from the ovary. ● Luteal phase: After ovulation, the corpus luteum forms and secretes progesterone and some estrogen. ● Progesterone stabilizes and further thickens the endometrium, making it suitable for implantation. ● If fertilization occurs, progesterone continues to support the uterine lining; if not, hormone levels drop, leading to menstruation. (1 mark) each for mentioning each phase (follicular, ovulation, luteal, and outcome) along with the specific hormone involved and its function.)
